walkthroughs.body_html: Dollard argued frustration (a blocked goal) leads to aggression. If the source cannot be attacked safely, aggression is displaced onto a target. Critics say not all frustration leads to aggression — context and learning matter too.

In large, anonymous groups (e.g. riots) people lose self-awareness. Reduced accountability and a focus on the group norm increase aggression. Zimbardo argued uniforms and masks accelerate deindividuation.

Biological theories (testosterone, amygdala) explain individual differences. Social theories (SLT, frustration) explain context and learning. Most psychologists argue an interactionist view — biology creates predisposition, environment triggers it.
